svg.text: one message, followed end-to-end · who does what, in which language, over which wire
INBOUND · a charging session event from the field
Real-world interaction. Car requests power. Charger confirms cable lock and protective earth.
IEC 61851 · analogue PWM over pilot line · no software in the loop
Zaptec Pro (AC charger) — vendor firmware on the wall
Decides: permission to charge, energy metering, fault detection. Opens a persistent WebSocket to Straumvakt on boot.
sends BootNotification, Heartbeat, StatusNotification, StartTransaction, MeterValues, StopTransaction
Charger phones home over encrypted WebSocket
OCPP 1.6J JSON-RPC framed messages over that socket
Cloudflare's global network — nearest EU point of presence
Terminates TLS, accepts the WebSocket upgrade, routes by hostname into the right Worker. No Straumvakt code runs here.
Edge hands the live socket to the OCPP Worker
internal routing, same region (weur) · no public hop
straumvakt-ocpp — traffic cop for charger connections
Authenticates the charger by its identity string, then looks up or spins up a Durable Object dedicated to that one charger.
Worker forwards to a Durable Object (one per charger)
typed RPC to DO.fetch() · deterministic id from identity string
5 · DURABLE OBJECT (one per OCPP Identity) — the brain
Holds the live WebSocket, session state, last N messages
For each incoming OCPP message, this DO:
1. validates envelope + payload with a Zod schema — malformed messages get a CallError, never reach storage
2. advances the charger's state machine (Available → Preparing → Charging → …)
3. translates OCPP-speak into domain events — StartTransaction → SessionStarted, MeterValues → MeterValueRecorded
DO posts a signed domain event to the main app
HTTPS POST · body: JSON domain event · header: x-straumvakt-ingest <shared secret>
HMAC-SHA256 signature over body + timestamp · idempotency key = OCPP message id
hlada — the Next.js app on Cloudflare Workers
Single transaction: verify signature and secret → check idempotency → append to event log → update projections.
• rejects replayed messages (same idempotency key → returns the cached result)
• writes to events.event_log first, then derives rows in charging.sessions, ocpp.connectors, etc.
Prisma turns TS calls into SQL
prisma client.edge + @prisma/adapter-neon · Neon's serverless WebSocket driver
Typed ORM — enforces the tenant boundary via withOrgContext()
Every query is tenant-scoped. A missing org_id throws before it ever reaches Postgres.
Parameterised SQL over Neon's WebSocket driver
INSERT into events, charging, ocpp — all inside one BEGIN/COMMIT
Source of truth — 17 Postgres schemas, branched per environment
The message now lives in three places, each playing a different role:
• events.event_log — the append-only history (this is the source of truth)
• charging.sessions / ocpp.connectors — "current view" projections, for fast reads
runtime: browser · language: HTML, CSS, rendered React
hlada Worker runs the server component
3. Repository returns typed data mapped from Prisma
React renders on the server, streams HTML + hydration payload back
hlada API route — writes to the outbox
returns 202 Accepted to the browser — command is durable now
Dispatches each to either OCPP (via DO) or vendor adapter, per routing_policy
Durable Object pushes OCPP message over the open socket
marks command row as 'sent', waits for CallResult
Vendor firmware cleanly ends the charging session, releases cable lock
Confirmation loops back through the inbound path
operator's next page load shows the charger as Available
The durable outbox is what keeps a crash-mid-dispatch from losing the command.

C / embedded (charger firmware) · TypeScript (everything Straumvakt owns) · Zod (message validation) · SQL (Neon) · HTML + React (UI) · OCPP 1.6J JSON-RPC (charger ↔ Straumvakt wire) · HMAC-SHA256 signed envelopes (gateway ↔ main app)
